key_insight: Patched Flow Matching learns a patch-local, inner-scaled prior from short-domain DNS and combines it with sparse sensors to reconstruct wall-pressure fields on much larger domains than seen in training.
engineering_relevance: This enables high-fidelity wall-pressure estimation for turbulent wall-bounded flows from very limited measurements, which is useful for sensing, control, and spectrum-aware flow diagnostics.
method: Train a patch-additive flow-matching model on short-domain DNS to capture local wall-pressure statistics.
Use training-free posterior sampling to assimilate sparse sensor data at inference.
Transfer to larger domains and higher Reynolds numbers via inner scaling and hierarchical fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate reconstruction on a domain 4× larger than training (16πδ vs 4πδ) using as little as 0.25% sensor coverage, across Reτ = 180, 500, and 1000.
watch_item: Performance depends on the validity of inner-scaling invariance and the availability of representative short-domain DNS patches; mismatch in physics or sensor placement could limit transfer.
paper_title: Patched Flow Matching: Generative Wall-Pressure Reconstruction Beyond Training-Domain Scales from Sparse Sensors
